players.product: gas turbines & SMR for data-center power

connects_to.relationship: Doosan Enerbility supplies forgings/materials for NuScale SMR modules and is bidding for module equipment manufacturing

contracts.signal: NuScale's 10-K states it has placed orders for long-lead items for the first twelve NuScale Power Module (NPM) upper reactor vessels - including forgings, tubing, tube bending machines and weld materials - with Doosan Enerbility, its manufacturing partner; manufacturing of long-lead materials forgings has progressed at Doosan Enerbility's manufacturing site, and manufacturing trials for other key components such as steam generator tubes and vessel cladding processes have been completed.
contracts.units: long-lead items for the first twelve NPM upper reactor vessels

players.product: SMR designer - Doosan Enerbility forging/material supplier and prospective module manufacturer

quarterly_data.signal: NuScale's 10-K says it has executed supply agreements with critical supply partners enabling it to order key NPM components, and names suppliers it expects to build NPM components - IHI Corporation, Precision Custom Components, Sarens Nuclear & Industrial Services and Curtiss-Wright - plus other key suppliers: Framatome (fuel assemblies), Honeywell International (control systems), Paragon Energy Solutions (protection systems), Sensia, Mirion Technologies and Weed Instruments dba Curtiss-Wright (sensors and instrumentation), ATS Industrial Automation (automation tooling and remote handling), Trillium Flow Technologies and Conval (valves) and PaR Systems (reactor building crane). Partners also include Fluor, Sargent & Lundy, JGC Holdings (EPC and commissioning of the first NuScale SMR-based plant), Samsung C&T (certain EPC activities) and GS Energy (project development in certain markets).

NuScale's one customer, RoPower Nuclear (a joint venture of Nuclearelectrica and Nova Power & Gas), is planning a power plant using NuScale's 6-unit 77 MWe NPM design at the Doicesti Power Station site in Romania. The 10-K describes the February 12, 2026 approval in two places: 'On February 12, 2026 the Nuclearelectrica Shareholders approved the investment decision for the SMR Project in Doicesti' and 'On February 12, 2026 the Romanian Government approved the investment decision for the Doicesti SMR plant project', allowing for the ability to seek secured financing for further site-specific design work. NuScale anticipates pre-EPC activities with an estimated duration of up to 15 months, including a Class 2 cost estimate, and has yet to commence negotiating definitive agreements related to its scopes.
quarterly_data.figure: 6-unit 77 MWe NPM plant; investment decision approved February 12, 2026; pre-EPC up to 15 months

quarterly_data.signal: During 2025 and 2024 NuScale entered into purchase commitments with supply chain partners for additional material to support and expedite development of future NPMs; the payments-due-by-year table (in thousands) shows materials purchase commitments for long-lead material of $48,867 ($6,929 due in 2026 and $41,938 in 2027) and supply chain readiness and manufacturing commitments of $12,382.
quarterly_data.figure: long-lead material purchase commitments $48,867 thousand ($6,929 thousand 2026; $41,938 thousand 2027); supply chain readiness and manufacturing $12,382 thousand
